subject: Dynamic Occupancy Model with Problem Seasons

messages.author: a9fad1a445e50f12
messages.subject: Dynamic Occupancy Model with Problem Seasons
parts:
Aloha,

I have a question about how to handle individual seasons with evidence of lack of fit in a dynamic occupancy model.

I am using the colext function to fit a dynamic occupancy model of pueo (Hawaiian short-eared owl) using eBird observations over a 10 year period. I conducted a MacKenzie Bailey goodness-of-fit test on the global model and found near evidence for lack of fit (p = 0.1) and a highish c-hat (1.83). (note: the GOF is a little preliminary since I ran the initial GOF test with 50 sims to get a general idea and estimate run time with more sims. the 50 sim run took 3.5hrs on 47 cores so it will take ~3 days for 1000 nsim or ~15 days for 5000 nsim)

With the preliminary GOF it appears the model fits the data reasonably well, albeit a bit overdispersed. When looking at the seasonal chi-square tables, however, I see that most seasons appear to fit pretty well, and one season in particular does not fit well (season 6, with 7 and 8 less not too far behind).

Questions:
  1. Is this cause for concern? And if so, what are some ways to improve fit in problem seasons? The col/ext parameters are informed with year and island in the global model.
  2. Would it be appropriate to proceed with model selection using QAIC and the c-hat estimated with 50 sims while the mb.gof.test runs over the next few days, given that the final model is provided the final c-hat when the run finishes?
